title_guess: India's exchange-rate history after Bretton Woods: pegged regime, NEER basket and LERMS

segments.teaches: under Bretton Woods (1944-1971) the dollar was tied to gold and other currencies to the dollar, a fixed exchange rate regime; it collapsed in 1971 when the US ended dollar convertibility, and India entered a pegged regime

elements.what: blue line 1944-1971 labelled with the system's name and a grey bar 1971-1992 labelled PEGGED REGIME
short note under the blue stretch about dollar-gold and dollar pegs
green [FIXED EXCHANGE RATE REGIME] label with a one-line definition
red cross at 1971 with a red 'collapsed' caption
cream cause box above the cross: dollar convertibility suspended

segments.notes: Cause box stacked above the event marker on a timeline.

segments.teaches: 1971-1975 the rupee was pegged to the pound sterling; from 1975 to 1992 it was pegged to a weighted basket of major trading partners' currencies

elements.what: bracket 1971-1975 with a dashed drop line
green banknote with a pound sign, captioned 'pegged to UK pound sterling'
long bracket 1975-1992 under the grey bar
basket explanation under the long bracket

segments.notes: Brackets under a timeline mark sub-periods.

segments.teaches: the basket held currencies of the main trading partners (Soviet Union, US, Japan, Germany, UK), and the rupee was pegged to it

elements.what: 1975-1992 pegged-regime strip moved to top left
cream highlight over the basket explanation
wicker basket full of mixed banknotes, reached by a curved arrow
ruled one-column list of the five partner countries
rope-like brown connector labelled PEGGED from the basket to a rupee banknote
green rupee banknote

segments.notes: Visual metaphor: the rupee note is literally tied to the basket by a rope.

segments.teaches: each partner currency has a weight in the basket (40/20/20/10/10) and a nominal exchange rate against the rupee

elements.what: basket icon at the table's top-left corner
countries x Weight x NER columns; weights then rates (e.g. 0.034 rouble per rupee) filled row by row

segments.notes: Running numeric example with real-looking historical rates; values typed in one row at a time.

segments.teaches: weight times rate for each currency, summed, gives the NEER (0.048 in the example)

elements.what: new working column ('40% of 0.034' -> result) with results in a blue highlighted column
blue vertical band over the results column
down-arrow from the column to the total 0.048

segments.notes: Weighted average computed in full on screen; the highlighted column is a reusable 'answer column' pattern.

segments.teaches: NEER means 0.048 units of the basket equal one rupee; NEER up means the rupee appreciated and the trade deficit worsens, NEER down means it depreciated and the deficit shrinks

elements.what: 0.048 x basket icon = rupee banknote inside a light-blue panel
NEER with its full name joined to the number by a stem
rounded red box for NEER rising and rounded blue dotted box for NEER falling, each under an underlined heading

segments.notes: Red/blue paired condition boxes reused later in this video and in E07.

segments.teaches: recap: in 1975-1992 the rupee was pegged to the NEER of its major trading partners

elements.what: pegged-regime strip and highlighted text at top left
curved arrow down to the basket
basket labelled NEER, tied by the rope connector to the rupee note
italic caption on a yellow band: of India's major trading partners

segments.notes: This composition is the video's 'home base' and is returned to three times.

segments.teaches: why peg to NEER: to stabilise the trade balance with major partners

elements.what: heading: what was the purpose?
yellow strip: NEER - pegged rope - rupee note
the red and blue NEER-up / NEER-down boxes slide in on the right
blue-outlined answer box under the strip

segments.notes: Question heading then answer; earlier boxes reused as evidence.

segments.teaches: the peg left the rupee misaligned; competitors such as China and Indonesia devalued against the dollar, India's exports lost competitiveness, and in 1991 the rupee was devalued in two steps

elements.what: statements stacked upward on the right, each with a wavy vertical line, joined by dotted red connectors (misalignment -> worse -> competitors devalue)
dark banner with red text at top right: export competitiveness suffered
blue dotted 1991 box linked by a curved line from the end of the timeline strip
home-base basket, rope and rupee note kept on the left

segments.notes: Chain builds bottom-up instead of top-down; returns to the home-base composition first.

elements.what: full 1944-1992 timeline with all labels restored
app promo overlay at bottom left (phone mock-up and store badges)

segments.notes: Mid-video promo overlay sits on top of the recap.

segments.teaches: big picture: fixed regime 1944-1992, floating since 1993, with LERMS (liberalised exchange rate management system) as the bridge in 1992-93

elements.what: green bar 1944-1992 and blue bar 1993-till date
green fixed-regime and blue floating-regime labels
bracket 1992-1993 with a dotted drop line
cream LERMS box with red expansion below

segments.notes: Simplified two-colour timeline as a closing summary.

elements.what: two next-video / playlist cards with loading bars
